name: Amanda Roy
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember comforting my baby with the rhythm of a delivery bike.” Friday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Amanda likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I used to do those drops while my baby slept in the sling. Now my baby earns more on his bicycle than I did.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Amanda has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with short black hair swept back. Amanda takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Amanda loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Amanda remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To document how the original family deliveries worked.
family: Vincent Trent is Amanda’s younger cousin. Amanda remembers the birthdays. Vincent asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A last ship together*, Vincent says, “I used to be their apprentice. I want them to stand back and see a lift go right without either of them directing it.”
connections: Harry Gill. A route drawn on paper gets checked against a carrier's years of actual door waits.
